scenes.say: Ever wonder why your DataFrame code is crawling? Let’s see how to speed it up and impress interviewers.
Using apply with custom functions runs row by row in Python. Vectorized operations, like multiplying a column directly, run in compiled code and are way faster.

scenes.label: Dtypes
scenes.sub: Choosing types like int32 or category cuts memory use.
scenes.say: Optimizing data types, like picking int thirty-two or category instead of object, can shrink memory use and boost speed.

scenes.label: Polars
scenes.sub: Polars is faster than pandas for big data.
scenes.say: Polars is a newer DataFrame library. It’s faster and more efficient than pandas for large datasets, thanks to its Rust backend.

scenes.question: What’s wrong with using apply?
scenes.wrong: It’s always fine for any size.
scenes.right: Apply is slow for big data. Vectorized ops are much faster.
scenes.say: Here’s a trap: What’s wrong with using apply on a huge DataFrame? It’s slow. Always go vectorized for speed.
